the ammonia chemical adsorption process on GaN(001) reconstructed surfaces can be predicted by SEAQT and the adsorption probabilities are dependent on the reconstructed surface and growth temperature.

ammonia chemical adsorption probabilities and temperature increases on GaN reconstructed surfaces are predicted using steepest entropy ascent quantum thermodynamics (DFT-SEAQT) under metalorganic vapor-phase epitaxy conditions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ammonia adsorption process on GaN(001) surfaces is a non-equilibrium process, and the probability of ammonia adsorption depends on the growth temperature, the reconstructed surface, and the ammonia concentration.
this study demonstrates the efficacy of SEAQT as a tool for understanding and controlling the non-equilibrium process of vapor-phase epitaxy.
the non-equilibrium process of the ammonia adsorption on the reconstructed surfaces is determined by the entropy production rate and the entropy change of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method for predicting the growth rate of GaN(000) surfaces in MOVPE based on a non-equilibrium process model.
DFT-SEAQ can be a powerful tool for the analysis of the non-equilibrium process of chemical adsorption under MOVPE condition, even when the state is far from equilibrium.
the DFT-SEAQt coupling can be applied to a wide range of non-equilibrium process modeling, including those that occur far from equilibrium, and the method is computationally efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the non-equilibrium adsorption process on reconstructed GaN(0002) surfaces is a function of the reconstructed surface type, growth temperature, and the heat of reaction.
the non-equilibrium thermodynamics approach is a viable alternative to microscopic-mesoscopic methods for modeling the MOVPE process.

the DFT-SEA QT approach provides a viable, first-principers based approach to the study of non-equilibrium process behavior, including the prediction of the probability of occurrence of a particular event in the process, the time evolution of the probability, the time evolution and temperature dependence of the heat of reaction, and the time evolution of entropy.
